text:
Mira: Heads up — I'm testing a new approach for quota/backpressure: a lightweight precheck + "slowdown" response headers. Idea is to avoid long server-side queueing for per-org bursts. Return semantics: 200 + X-Redwood-Slowdown when we accept but need the client to back off, 429 for hard per-key/org limit, and 503 when global runtime is overloaded (circuit-breaker). Open to feedback.

alex: Quick q — what should SDKs do on X-Redwood-Slowdown? Sleep locally before sending the next token chunk? Some clients might ignore it.

Mira: Yes, SDKs would interpret X-Redwood-Slowdown (ms) as a suggestion to delay subsequent requests/streams. If the header is present the client should back off for that many ms. We still complete the request.

sandeep: Concern: returning 200 for slowed responses changes how callers detect rate limiting. Many infra teams expect 429 for any rate control. Could we include both a header and a quasi-status? e.g. 200 + header + X-Redwood-Quota-State: slowed|ok|throttled ?

jess: From a telemetry + console POV we need metrics: slowdown_count, slowdown_ms_histogram, throttled_count (429), rejected_count (503), and precheck_failures. Console should surface a tiny banner: "Your traffic is being slowed — expected extra latency" with links to fix (increase reserved capacity / lower concurrency).

tim: SDK semantics matter. If we return 200 for slowed requests, app authors might never notice. I prefer 202 Accepted when we accept but will queue/process later, or 409? 202 signals "work accepted" but not completed. Thoughts?

Mira: 202 implies async semantics (i.e., client poll). We want to avoid forcing client to poll. The goal is to keep synchronous responses but signal that downstream may be delayed. So 200+header seems better UX for sync paths. But agree we need unmistakable signals for ops/console.

alex: Could we add a Retry-After header when slowdown is >= threshold? Many HTTP libraries will honor Retry-After for retries. That might complement X-Redwood-Slowdown.

sandeep: Example response proposal:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Slowdown: 150  # milliseconds client should delay next request
X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 12
X-Redwood-Quota-State: slowed
Cache-Control: no-store

{ "id": "resp_...", "choices": [...] }
```
And for hard throttle:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-Redwood-Quota-State: throttled
{ "error": {"type":"quota_exceeded","message":"per-org rate limit"}}
```
For global overload:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Retry-After: 10
X-Redwood-Quota-State: unavailable
{ "error": {"type":"service_unavailable","message":"runtime overloaded"}}
```
```

jess: Perfect — that maps cleanly to dashboards and alerting. We should also tag traces/spans with quota_state and slowdown_ms so SLO dashboards can slice.

tim: Also think about rollout: start with precheck endpoint only. /v1/precheck returns whether a request would be accepted and suggested slowdown. That avoids surprising live traffic while we iterate on client SDKs.

Mira: Agreed. Plan:
- Phase 0: precheck endpoint + dashboard tiles for precheck pass/fail rates (canary to internal orgs).
- Phase 1: implement X-Redwood-Slowdown header on a config flag for a small percent of traffic, add Retry-After heuristics, instrument slowdown metrics.
- Phase 2: expand to broader rollout + SDK support + console UX changes.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert - cb:runtime-global: circuit-breaker entered degraded state (10:42) — auto-shed = true

alex: Nice timing :) ops-bot shows why we need the 503 path. For precheck, let's define input: org_id, desired_tokens, model_hint, priority. Response: accept|slowdown|reject + suggested_retry_seconds.

sandeep: I'll draft a short RFC with header names, precheck schema, metric names, and a suggested SDK backoff impl. Will ping owners for Console + SDK to coordinate.

jess: I'll add dashboard mockups (tiny card: slowed requests / throttled requests / avg slowdown ms) and a console message template.

Mira: Action items captured. Thanks — please keep replies short if you want specific API names in the RFC.

alex: One more: for model-fallback behavior, can we auto-route to a compatible lower-cost quantized model when org is throttled instead of rejecting? That could reduce 429s. Might be more complex but high ROI.

Mira: Good idea — add 'fallback_model' field to precheck response so router can decide. I'll include that in the RFC.

sandeep: Cool. RFC ETA EOD Friday, canary next week for internal orgs.

Mira: Thanks team :thumbsup:
